title: Sequence Models
tagline: Recurrent networks, LSTMs, sequence-to-sequence models and the invention of attention
summary: Language unfolds in time. This course models sequences with recurrent networks, meets the difficulty of long-range dependencies with LSTMs and GRUs, builds sequence-to-sequence models for translation, and introduces attention — the idea that became the Transformer.

overview: Before transformers, sequence models were RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs. This course covers recurrent architectures, the vanishing gradient problem, and sequence-to-sequence learning.
The key insight is that LSTMs solved gradient flow with gating; attention solved the bottleneck of fixed-length encoding.
outcomes: Trace the RNN and LSTM forward/backward pass.
Explain the vanishing gradient problem and how gating solves it.
Describe sequence-to-sequence with attention and the encoder-decoder architecture.
Analyze GRU vs. LSTM and when recurrent models suffice.
